{{Short description|Indian-born electrical engineer and applied physicist}}

[[File:SandipTiwari2021.jpg|alt=Sandip Tiwari|thumb|Sandip Tiwari]]
'''Sandip Tiwari''' is an Indian-born electrical engineer and applied physicist. He is the Charles N. Mellowes Professor of Engineering at [[Cornell University]]. His previous roles were director of National Nanotechnology Users Network, director of the [[National Nanotechnology Infrastructure Network]], and research scientist at [[Thomas J. Watson Research Center|IBM T. J. Watson Research Center]]. He is best known for his pioneering research in the fields of SiGe transistor and nanocrystal memory.{{Citation needed|date=July 2022}}

== Early life and education ==
Sandip Tiwari was born in Ahmedabad, India, and received his BTech from [[Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur]] in 1976. He received his M.Eng. at [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]] and PhD at [[Cornell University]] in 1980.{{Citation needed|date=July 2022}}

== Work and academic career ==
His early research career was at [[IBM]]'s Research Division until 1999. During this period, he did the early work on compound semiconductor transistors and co-developed the first SiGe transistor.<ref>S.S. Iyer, G.L. Patton, S.S. Delage, S. Tiwari, J.M.C. Stork, "Silicon-germanium base heterojunction bipolar transistors by molecular beam epitaxy", International Electron Devices Meeting (1987).</ref><ref>G.L. Patton, S.S. Iyer, S.L. Delage, S. Tiwari and J.M.C. Stork, “Silicon-Germanium Base Heterojunction Bipolar Transistors by Molecular Beam Epitaxy,” [[IEEE Electron Device Letters]], EDL-9, No. 4, p. 165 (1988)</ref> He also pioneered various quantum and nanoscale devices, such as the nanocrystal memory.<ref>S. Tiwari, F. Rana, H. Hanafi, A. Hartstein, E. Crabbe and K. Chan, “A Silicon Nano-Crystals Based Memory,” Applied Physics Letters, 68, p.1377, 4 Mar. (1996)</ref> The first demonstration of SiGe transistor was honored as IEEE [[International Electron Devices Meeting]] (IEDM) Top Industry Innovation of 1987.{{Citation needed|date=July 2022}} His work on nanocrystal memory was one of the 50 most-cited papers in the history of Applied Physics Letters in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.numse.nagoya-u.ac.jp/F5/k-ueda/APL-mostcited-paper-2013.pdf|title=Celebrating 50 Years of Applied Physics Letters|website=Numse.nagoya-u.ac.jp|access-date=17 July 2022}}</ref>

At [[Cornell University]], his Nanoscale ElectroScience Research Group<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.duffield.cornell.edu/people/sandip-tiwari/|title=Sandip Tiwari &#124; Cornell Engineering|website=Engineering.cornell.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://electroscience.ece.cornell.edu/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090302152034/http://electroscience.ece.cornell.edu/|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 2, 2009|title=Nanoscale ElectroScience Research Group, ECE Cornell|website=electroscience.ece.cornell.edu}}</ref> focused on adaptive approaches for low power design,<ref>J. Y. Kim, P. Solomon and S. Tiwari, “Adaptive Circuit Design Using Independently Biased Back-Gated Double-Gate MOSFETS,” IEEE Circuits and Systems I, 59 (4), Apr.., 806-819(2012)</ref> three-dimensional integration,<ref>L. Xue, C. C. Liu, H.-S. Kim, S (K) Kim, and S. Tiwari, “Three-Dimensional Integration: Technology, Use, and Issues for Mixed-Signal Applications,” IEEE Transactions on Electron Devices, 50, No. 3, 601-609(2003)
</ref><ref>C. C. Liu, I. Ganusov, M. Burtscher, and S. Tiwari, “Bridging the Processor-Memory Performance Gap with 3D IC Technology,” IEEE Design and Test of Computers, Vol. 22, Nov., 556-564(2005)
</ref> inexact computing,<ref>J. Y. Kim and S. Tiwari, “Inexact Computing using Probabilistic Circuits: Ultra Low-Power Digital Processing”, ACM Journal of Emerging Technologies, Vol. 10, No. 2, Article 16, February (2014)</ref> and Bayesian implementations<ref>S. Tiwari and D. Querlioz, “On the physical underpinnings of the unusual effectiveness of probabilistic and neural computation,” Invited paper, Tech. Dig. of IEEE Int’l Conf. on Rebooting Computing, 1--4(2017)</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ieeetv.ieee.org/on-the-physical-underpinnings-of-the-unusual-effectiveness-of-probabilistic-and-neural-computation-ieee-rebooting-computing-2017|title=On the Physical Underpinnings of the Unusual Effectiveness of Probabilistic and Neural Computation - IEEE Rebooting Computing 2017|website=[[IEEE]] |date=8 December 2017 }}</ref>

* Life Fellow of [[IEEE]], 1994<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://services27.ieee.org/fellowsdirectory/getdetailprofile.html?custNum=x92aFsS3hFpUK4GhzPZUYQ==&bccaptions=Alphabetical+Listing+&bclocations=/fellowsdirectory/home.html|title=IEEE Fellows Directory - Member Profile|website=[[IEEE]]}}</ref>
